summary:
Calabarzon is a region of the Philippines and stands under the national framework. Its own legal layer consists of local anti-discrimination ordinances in four units: Batangas province (2015), Cavite (2014 to 2018, later extended to cover gender identity), Batangas City (2016) and Calamba (2017). No regional-level statute is identified. For a trans visitor, protection depends on which city or municipality they are in, and the ordinances are the only region-specific protection mechanism the sources identify.

On 13 August 2025 a Philippine daily reported the murder of an LGBTQ pageant winner in Batangas. The victim, crowned in Lipa City days earlier, sustained 13 stab wounds, and police work the case as a homicide. The report states no arrest, no motive and no finding that the killing was bias-related, and does not say whether the victim was transgender. One killing does not establish a rate, and the sources carry no general homicide figure for the region against which it could be compared.
tangentialFactors:
The killing occurred in Batangas, one of the four Calabarzon units with a local anti-discrimination ordinance. The sources record no prosecution or enforcement outcome after it, so what the ordinances achieve in practice against violence directed at LGBTQ people in the region is not established.

The four ordinances were adopted between 2014 and 2017, and Cavite's was later amended to cover gender identity. Coverage is not uniform across the region, and the sources identify no regional-level instrument that would apply in units without their own ordinance.
localsOnly: Residents of Calabarzon depend on municipal and provincial ordinances rather than a regional statute. The sources identify four: Batangas province (2015), Cavite (2014 to 2018, later extended to cover gender identity), Batangas City (2016) and Calamba (2017). Cavite's extension to gender identity is the only change in scope the sources record.
outOfScopeNotes:
The August 2025 killing in Lipa City is unresolved in the sources: no arrest, no stated motive and no finding that it was bias-related are reported, and the reports do not state whether the victim was transgender. Whether the case is counted in any wider tally is not established.

The sources do not establish whether Calabarzon units other than Batangas province, Cavite, Batangas City and Calamba have anti-discrimination ordinances, how the four identified ordinances are enforced, what penalties they carry, or whether complaints have been filed under them. No regional-level statute is identified. No general homicide figure for the region appears in the sources, so the single killing cannot be placed against a background rate.
